description: DESIGN TALK (trust model). From review of ag-s99.4 (2026-10-14). Since deployments are created by their first valid run, the GitHub App installation is the only gate. If the App is public (installable by anyone), any GitHub user can install it on their own repo, mint an OIDC token with Agbredo's audience, and create deployments and send telemetry. The README now requires the App to be installable 'Only on this account'. Option for defence in depth: compare the installation's account.login / account.id (already in the GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/installation response, see internal/github/github.go Installation) with an allowlist env var such as AGBREDO_ALLOWED_OWNERS, refusing with 403 otherwise. Questions for Matt: is the production App private today? Is an allowlist wanted, and by login or by id? Check: go test ./... with AGBREDO_TEST_DATABASE_URL.

comments.text: 2026-10-15 discussion with Matt. Matt's idea: use the same list as AGBREDO_ADMIN_USERS as the allowlist. Concerns noted: (1) Admin users are people who log in to the dashboard. The installation account (account.login) is the repo owner, which can be a user or an org. If repos belong to an org (the usual enterprise case), the org name would have to go in AGBREDO_ADMIN_USERS, mixing two meanings and letting a user account with that name pass the login check. (2) Match by login or by id? Logins can be renamed or re-registered; ids are stable but hard to read. Suggested login, with the weakness noted in docs. (3) Suggested option: new AGBREDO_ALLOWED_OWNERS that falls back to AGBREDO_ADMIN_USERS when unset. Single shared list is also acceptable if docs say org names go in the admin list. Open questions for Matt: do the agent repos belong to a personal account or an org? Is the production App private today (README requires 'Only on this account')? Login or id? Shared list or separate variable with fallback? DECISION: postponed. No code changes made.

title: Restrict which GitHub accounts may create deployments
